To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
τ + τ − production in nucleus– nucleus collisions can be used as an alternative to e + e − and μ + μ − production in order to study the QGP at the LHC.

the Drell–Yann contribution is expected to dominate over the thermal contribution for τ + τ – pair mass in the range 4–20 GeV at LHC energies, and that the τ + τ – ratio for Pb + P Pb scaled by number of collisions is significantly above unity in the mass range 3–6 GeV.
the τ + τ - pair production in nucleus-nucleus collisions can be a useful probe to study the QGP properties.

the study of the heavy lepton pair production from QGP and the comparison with the Drell–Yann process at LHC energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
τ + τ − yield is a sensitive probe to study the QGP at LHC energy.

, in the mass window M ( τ + τ − ) = 4 – 6 GeV, the τ + τ - production in Pb + Pb collisions at the LHC is dominated by the Drell-Yan processes, while in the mass window, M ( τ +τ − ) = 6 – 20 GeV, the Drell-Yann process dominates the production from QGP.
the τ + τ – pair production from QGP in the mass window (4–6) GeV can be detected at the LHC energies.

, τ lepton pair production from QGP can be observed at LHC energies for M (τ + τ − ) ⩽ 10 GeV, which is a unique feature for the QGP.
the τ lepton pair production from the Drell–Yann process dominates over thermal partonic source contribution for τ pair mass from 2 to 20 Gev at the LHC energies.
the study of τ + and τ − leptons can be a powerful probe of the QGP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the τ lepton pairs from quark–anti quark annihilation via virtual photon, Z or Higgs boson are more sensitive probes of the QGP than the e + e − and μ + μ − pairs.
the τ + τ – pair production from QGP can be distinguished from the hadronic contribution in the M window 4 ⋍ M (GeV) < 10 at LHC energy.
